questions.explanation: Àyọkà sọ pé ó ń gbé ní Ìbàdàn (He lives in Ibadan).

questions.explanation: "Àgbẹ̀ ni bàbá rẹ̀" — his father is a farmer.

Kí ni Bọ́lá máa ń ṣe ní àràárọ̀ kí ó tó lọ sí ilé-ìwé?

Ó máa ń lọ sí oko
Ó máa ń gbá ilẹ̀, ó sì máa ń pọn omi
questions.explanation: Every morning he sweeps and fetches water before school.

Kí ló dé tí Bọ́lá fi fẹ́ràn ìwé kíkà?
questions.explanation: He loves reading because he wants to become a doctor.

questions.stem: Mélòó ni fáwẹ̀lì àìránmúpè (oral vowels) tí ó wà nínú èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: The oral vowels are a, e, ẹ, i, o, ọ, u.

questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni fáwẹ̀lì àránmúpè (nasal vowel)?
questions.explanation: Nasal vowels are written with n: an, ẹn, in, ọn, un.

questions.stem: Mélòó ni fáwẹ̀lì àránmúpè tí a ń kọ nínú èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: They are an, ẹn, in, ọn, un.

questions.stem: Which of these letters is NOT found in the Yoruba alphabet?
questions.explanation: Yoruba has no c, q, v, x or z.

questions.stem: Kọ́ńsónáǹtì wo ni a fi ètè méjèèjì pè (bilabial)?
questions.explanation: /b/ and /m/ are made with both lips.

questions.stem: Ohùn mélòó ni ó wà nínú èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Yoruba has three tones: high (òkè), mid (àárín) and low (ìsàlẹ̀).

questions.stem: Àmì ohùn tí a fi ń kọ ohùn òkè (high tone) ni
questions.explanation: The high tone is marked with an acute accent, e.g. mí.

questions.stem: Ohùn wo ni a kì í sábà fi àmì sí lórí?
questions.explanation: The mid tone is usually left unmarked.

questions.stem: Nínú "dò, re, mí", ohùn wo ni "dò" dúró fún?
questions.explanation: dò = low, re = mid, mí = high.

questions.stem: Sílébù mélòó ni ó wà nínú ọ̀rọ̀ "ọmọ"?
questions.explanation: ọ-mọ: two syllables (V + CV).

questions.stem: Ìhun sílébù wo ni kò sí nínú èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Yoruba syllables are open: V, CV or N; there are no closed syllables.

questions.stem: Sílébù mélòó ni ó wà nínú ọ̀rọ̀ "aṣọ"?
questions.explanation: a-ṣọ: two syllables.

questions.stem: Akọtọ́ túmọ̀ sí
options: ọ̀nà tí a gbà ń kọ èdè sílẹ̀ (orthography)
questions.explanation: Akọtọ́ is the agreed way of spelling/writing a language.

questions.stem: Ní akọtọ́ òde òní, a ń kọ "aiye" gẹ́gẹ́ bí
questions.explanation: Modern orthography writes ayé, not aiye.

questions.stem: Ní akọtọ́ òde òní, a ń kọ "Oshogbo" gẹ́gẹ́ bí
questions.explanation: The sound "sh" is written as ṣ in modern Yoruba orthography.

questions.stem: Ní akọtọ́ òde òní, ọ̀nà wo ni a gbà ń kọ "nigbati"?
questions.explanation: Word division: nígbà tí is written as two words today.

questions.stem: Ọdún wo ni ìpinnu ìjọba àpapọ̀ lórí akọtọ́ Yorùbá tí a ń lò lónìí wáyé?
questions.explanation: The 1974 decision followed the work of the Joint Consultative Committee.

questions.stem: Ní akọtọ́ òde òní, a ń kọ "enia" gẹ́gẹ́ bí
questions.explanation: The old spelling enia is now ènìyàn.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe (verb)?
questions.explanation: jẹ (eat) is a verb.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ (noun)?
questions.explanation: ajá (dog) is a noun.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-àpèjúwe (adjective)?
questions.explanation: dúdú (black) describes a noun.

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn "Adé lọ sí ọjà", ọ̀rọ̀-atọ́kùn (preposition) ni
questions.explanation: sí (to) is the preposition.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ọ̀rọ̀-àsopọ̀ (conjunction)?
questions.explanation: tàbí (or), àti (and) and ṣùgbọ́n (but) are conjunctions.

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ "olùkọ́" ni a ṣẹ̀dá láti ara ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe
questions.explanation: olù- + kọ́ = olùkọ́ (teacher).

questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí ni ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ aṣẹ̀dá (derived noun)?
questions.explanation: oní- + iṣẹ́ = oníṣẹ́ (worker); the others are basic (àìṣẹ̀dá) nouns.

questions.stem: Kí ni a fi kún "rìn" láti ṣẹ̀dá "ìrìn"?
questions.explanation: Prefix ì- + rìn (walk) = ìrìn (walk/journey).

questions.topic: Ise oro aropo oruko ninu gbolohun
questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀-arọ́pò-orúkọ "wọ́n" túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: wọ́n/àwọn = they.

questions.topic: Ise oro aropo oruko ninu gbolohun
questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn "Mo rí i", "Mo" jẹ́
questions.explanation: Mo (I) is the subject of the verb rí.

questions.topic: Ise oro aropo oruko ninu gbolohun
questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn "Olùkọ́ nà wọ́n", "wọ́n" jẹ́
questions.explanation: wọ́n receives the action of nà (beat), so it is the object.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is "Adé jẹun, ṣùgbọ́n Bọ́lá kò jẹun"?
questions.explanation: Two clauses joined by ṣùgbọ́n make a compound sentence.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is "Ọmọ tí ó ń sunkún ti sùn"?
questions.explanation: The relative clause "tí ó ń sunkún" is embedded, making it complex.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is "Adé ra ẹja"?
questions.explanation: It has one verb and one clause.

questions.stem: Orí-ọ̀rọ̀ àròkọ ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Àkọlé is the title of the essay.

questions.stem: Apá àròkọ tí a fi ń ṣe ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Ìfáàrà is the introduction.

questions.stem: Apá ìparí àròkọ ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Ìgúnlẹ̀ is the conclusion.

questions.stem: Kí ni "ìlapa èrò" nínú àròkọ kíkọ?
options: Orúkọ ẹni tí ó kọ àròkọ
Ètò àwọn kókó tí a fẹ́ kọ nípa rẹ̀ kí a tó kọ àròkọ
questions.explanation: It is the outline/plan of the points before writing.

questions.stem: Lẹ́tà tí a kọ sí ọ̀rẹ́ tàbí ẹbí ni lẹ́tà
questions.explanation: An informal letter is written to a friend or relative.

questions.stem: Lẹ́tà tí akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ kọ sí ọ̀gá ilé-ìwé láti tọrọ àyè jẹ́ lẹ́tà
questions.explanation: Letters to officials are formal.

questions.stem: Kí ni ìyàtọ̀ pàtàkì kan láàárín lẹ́tà gbẹ̀fẹ́ àti lẹ́tà àìgbẹ̀fẹ́?
options: Lẹ́tà àìgbẹ̀fẹ́ ní àdírẹ́sì méjì (ti olùkọ̀wé àti ti ẹni tí a kọ ọ́ sí)
questions.explanation: A formal letter carries both the writer's and the receiver's addresses.

questions.stem: "Ogún" túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: Ogún = 20.

questions.stem: "Ọgbọ̀n" túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: Ọgbọ̀n = 30.

questions.stem: "Ogójì" túmọ̀ sí
"Ọ̀kàndínlógún" túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: Ọ̀kàn-dín-ní-ogún = one less than twenty = 19.

questions.stem: "Igba" (gẹ́gẹ́ bí òǹkà) túmọ̀ sí
"Ọgọ́rùn-ún" túmọ̀ sí
"Ẹgbàá" túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: Ẹgbàá = 2,000.

questions.stem: Lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn ni lítíréṣọ̀ tí
options: a ń wò lórí tẹlifíṣọ̀n nìkan
a ń fi ẹnu sọ láti ìrandíran, kì í ṣe èyí tí a kọ sílẹ̀
questions.explanation: Oral literature is passed down by word of mouth.

questions.stem: Ewì àwọn ọdẹ tí a fi ń júbà Ògún ni
questions.explanation: Hunters chant ìjálá in honour of Ògún.

questions.stem: Ewì tí ìyàwó máa ń sun nígbà tí ó bá ń kúrò nílé bàbá rẹ̀ lọ sí ilé ọkọ ni
questions.explanation: Ẹkún ìyàwó (bride's chant) is a non-religious (àìjẹmẹ́sìn) oral poem.

questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni ìṣeré ajẹmẹ́sìn (religious oral performance)?
questions.explanation: Ẹ̀sẹ Ifá is chanted in Ifá worship; the others are social.

questions.stem: Ewì alohùn tí a fi ń yin ènìyàn tàbí ìdílé rẹ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Oríkì is praise poetry for a person or lineage.

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí a gbà gbọ́ pé ó ní agbára láti mú kí nǹkan ṣẹlẹ̀ (incantation) ni
questions.explanation: Ọfọ̀ is incantation believed to have power.

questions.stem: Òwe jẹ́
options: ọ̀rọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ tí ó kún fún ọgbọ́n
questions.explanation: Proverbs carry the wisdom of the elders.

questions.stem: Àwọn tí ó kópa nínú ìtàn tàbí eré ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Ẹ̀dá-ìtàn are the characters.

questions.stem: Ibi àti àkókò tí ìtàn ti ṣẹlẹ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Ibùdó-ìtàn is the setting.

questions.stem: Bí òǹkọ̀wé ṣe tò ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ inú ìtàn tẹ̀léra wọn ni
questions.explanation: Àhunpọ̀-ìtàn is the plot.

questions.stem: Èrò pàtàkì tí òǹkọ̀wé fẹ́ kí òǹkàwé mọ̀ nínú ìtàn ni
questions.explanation: Kókó-ọ̀rọ̀ is the theme.

questions.stem: Eré-onítàn (drama) jẹ́ lítíréṣọ̀ tí a kọ láti
questions.explanation: Drama is written to be acted on stage.

questions.stem: "Ọmọ náà ga bí igi ọ̀pẹ" jẹ́ àpẹẹrẹ
questions.explanation: The comparison uses "bí" (like), so it is a simile.

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà-èdè tí a fi ń sọ ohun kan kọjá bí ó ṣe rí gan-an ni
questions.explanation: Àsọdùn is exaggeration (hyperbole).

questions.topic: Asayan iwe: itan aroso oloro geere
questions.stem: Ìtàn àròsọ ni ìtàn tí
options: ó ṣẹlẹ̀ gan-an nínú ìtàn ilẹ̀ Yorùbá
òǹkọ̀wé hùmọ̀ láti inú ọpọlọ rẹ̀
questions.explanation: A novel/prose fiction is created from the writer's imagination.

questions.stem: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìtàn, ta ni baba ńlá àwọn Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Odùduwà is regarded as the progenitor of the Yoruba.

questions.stem: Ìlú wo ni a gbà gbọ́ pé ó jẹ́ orírun àwọn Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Ilé-Ifẹ̀ is regarded as the cradle of the Yoruba.

questions.stem: Àwọn Ẹ̀gbá ni a mọ̀ jùlọ pẹ̀lú ìlú
questions.explanation: Abẹ́òkúta is the main Ẹ̀gbá town.

questions.stem: Iléṣà jẹ́ olú-ìlú àwọn
questions.explanation: Iléṣà is the chief town of the Ìjẹ̀ṣà.

questions.stem: Ẹni tí ó máa ń ṣe alárinà láàárín ìdílé ọkọ àti ìyàwó nínú ìgbéyàwó ìbílẹ̀ ni
questions.explanation: The alárinà is the go-between in traditional marriage.

questions.stem: Which of these is a form of modern marriage among the Yoruba?
options: Marriage at a court registry, church or mosque
Marriage with no family involvement at all
Marriage decided by the Ọba alone
questions.explanation: The syllabus contrasts traditional marriage with court, church and mosque weddings.

questions.stem: Ẹni tí àwọn Yorùbá gbà gbọ́ pé ó ga jùlọ nínú ẹ̀sìn ìbílẹ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Olódùmarè (Ọlọ́run) is the Supreme Being.

questions.stem: Òrìṣà ààrá àti mànàmáná ni
questions.explanation: Ṣàngó is linked with thunder and lightning.

questions.stem: Òrìṣà irin tí àwọn ọdẹ àti alágbẹ̀dẹ ń bọ ni
questions.explanation: Ògún is the deity of iron.

questions.topic: Atunyewo esin ibile Yoruba siwaju si: ohun mimo
questions.stem: Àwọ̀ aṣọ wo ni àwọn olùsìn Ọbàtálá máa ń wọ̀ láti fi hàn pé òrìṣà mímọ́ ni?
questions.explanation: Ọbàtálá is associated with white cloth (aṣọ funfun) and purity.

questions.stem: Ogun Kíríjì wáyé láàárín Ìbàdàn àti
questions.explanation: The Kíríjì war was fought between Ìbàdàn and the Ẹ̀kìtì Parapọ̀ alliance.

questions.stem: Which of these was a traditional Yoruba weapon of war?
questions.explanation: Traditional weapons included ọfà, idà (sword) and ìbọn (gun).

questions.stem: Orúkọ tí a ń sọ ọmọ tí ó kọ́kọ́ jáde nínú ìbejì ni
questions.explanation: Táíwò is the first twin; Kẹ́hìndé the second.

questions.stem: Orúkọ tí a máa ń sọ ọmọ tí ó fi ẹsẹ̀ wáyé nígbà ìbí ni
questions.explanation: Ìgè is born feet first — an orúkọ àmútọ̀runwá.

questions.stem: Kí ni ìdí tí a fi ń lo oyin níbi ìsọmọlórúkọ?
options: Kí ọmọ náà lè ní ọ̀pọ̀ ọmọ
Kí ọmọ náà lè gbọ́n ju ìyá rẹ̀ lọ
Kí ayé ọmọ náà lè dùn
questions.explanation: Honey symbolises a sweet life.

questions.stem: Orúkọ bí Àlàbí, Àkànbí àti Àdùkẹ́ jẹ́
questions.explanation: These are praise names (oríkì).

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà ìrànra-ẹni-lọ́wọ́ tí ọ̀pọ̀ ènìyàn fi ń bá ẹnì kan ṣiṣẹ́ ńlá kan lọ́jọ́ kan (bí oko ríro) ni
questions.explanation: Ọ̀wẹ̀ is communal labour to help one person.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes àjọ (thrift contribution)?
options: Members never get their money back
It is a type of war
Members save money regularly with a collector and collect it later
questions.explanation: Àjọ is a traditional savings system.

questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni ìwà ìkà sí ọmọnìkejì lóde òní?
questions.explanation: Kidnapping is cruelty against others.

questions.stem: Ibi tí a ti ń ra nǹkan tí a sì ń tà á ni
questions.explanation: Ọjà is the market.

questions.stem: Ẹni tí ó ń ṣe iṣẹ́ irin (fífi irin rọ ọkọ́ àti àdá) ni
questions.explanation: The alágbẹ̀dẹ is the blacksmith.

questions.stem: If both parents have the AS genotype, which genotype may some of their children have that causes sickle cell disease?
questions.explanation: Two AS parents have a 1 in 4 chance of an SS child in each pregnancy.

questions.stem: Àrokò jẹ́
options: ọ̀nà ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ àtijọ́ tí a fi ohun èlò rán ẹnì kan níṣẹ́
questions.explanation: Àrokò is coded communication with objects.

questions.stem: Mélòó ni lẹ́tà tí ó wà nínú álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: The Yoruba alphabet has 25 letters.

questions.stem: Mélòó ni kọ́ńsónáǹtì tí ó wà nínú álífábẹ́ẹ̀tì Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: 25 letters − 7 vowels = 18 consonants.

questions.stem: What is the Yoruba word for "red"?
questions.explanation: pupa = red; funfun = white; dúdú = black.

questions.topic: Oruko won eniyan ati bi won se je si ara won (L2)
questions.stem: What is the Yoruba word for "mother"?
questions.explanation: ìyá = mother; bàbá = father.

questions.topic: Oruko won eniyan ati bi won se je si ara won (L2)
questions.stem: "Àbúrò" means
questions.explanation: Àbúrò = younger sibling; ẹ̀gbọ́n = elder sibling.

questions.stem: What is the Yoruba word for "dog"?
questions.explanation: ajá = dog; ológbò = cat; ewúrẹ́ = goat; adìẹ = chicken.

questions.stem: "Erin" in Yoruba is the name of which animal?
questions.explanation: erin = elephant; kìnnìún = lion; ẹkùn = leopard; ọ̀bọ = monkey.

questions.stem: Which of these is a fruit tree?
questions.explanation: Ọsàn (orange) bears fruit; ìrókò is a timber tree.

questions.topic: Oruko awon nnkan ti o wa ni ayika wa (L2)
questions.stem: What is the Yoruba word for "water"?
questions.explanation: omi = water; iná = fire; igi = tree; ilé = house.

questions.stem: What is the Yoruba word for "head"?
questions.explanation: orí = head; ẹsẹ̀ = leg; ọwọ́ = hand; etí = ear.

questions.stem: We see with our
questions.explanation: ojú = eyes; imú = nose; etí = ear; ẹnu = mouth.

questions.topic: Awon ipede ti a maa n so ti a ba n gba alejo (L2)
questions.stem: To welcome a visitor, a Yoruba speaker says:
questions.explanation: Ẹ kú àbọ̀ (or Ẹ káàbọ̀) means "welcome".

questions.topic: Sise amulo orisirisi gbolohun fun ibeere ati idahun (L2)
questions.stem: Which question word means "Where?"
questions.explanation: Níbo = where; Ta ni = who; Kí ni = what; Mélòó = how many.

questions.topic: Sise amulo orisirisi gbolohun fun ibeere ati idahun (L2)
questions.stem: "Ta ni ó wá?" is asking
questions.explanation: Ta ni = who.

questions.stem: "Ebi ń pa mí" means
questions.explanation: Ebi = hunger; òùngbẹ = thirst.

questions.stem: Àlọ́ àpamọ̀ is
options: a riddle that the listeners must answer
questions.explanation: Àlọ́ àpamọ̀ are riddles; àlọ́ àpagbè are folktales with songs.

questions.stem: Àlọ́ àpagbè differs from àlọ́ àpamọ̀ because àlọ́ àpagbè
options: is a short question with a one-word answer
is a story, usually with songs, that teaches a moral
questions.explanation: Àlọ́ àpagbè are folktales; àlọ́ àpamọ̀ are riddles.

questions.stem: Children's moonlight songs and games are usually performed
options: in the evening under the moonlight
questions.explanation: Moonlight games such as Bojúbojú are played in the evening.

questions.stem: Short children's rhymes and poems are mainly used to
options: teach children language, values and counting in a fun way
questions.explanation: Ewì ọmọdé help children learn while playing.

questions.stem: What is "ẹ̀ta" (in counting) in English?
questions.explanation: ọ̀kan 1, èjì 2, ẹ̀ta 3, ẹ̀rin 4, àrún 5.

questions.stem: What is "ẹ̀wá"?
questions.explanation: ẹ̀fà 6, èje 7, ẹ̀jọ 8, ẹ̀sán 9, ẹ̀wá 10.

questions.topic: Ikini ni oniruuru akoko ati asiko (L2)
questions.stem: Which greeting is used in the morning?
questions.explanation: Ẹ káàárọ̀ = good morning; Ẹ káàsán = good afternoon; Ẹ kúùrọ̀lẹ́ = good evening; Ó dàárọ̀ = good night.

questions.topic: Ikini ni oniruuru akoko ati asiko (L2)
questions.stem: How do you greet someone who is working?
questions.explanation: Ẹ kú iṣẹ́ = well done (at work).

questions.topic: Akoko ati asiko: ojo ati osu (L2)
questions.stem: Which day is "Àìkú" in English?
questions.explanation: Àìkú is Sunday; Ajé is Monday.

questions.topic: Akoko ati asiko: ojo ati osu (L2)
questions.stem: Which day is "Ọjọ́rú"?
questions.explanation: Ìṣẹ́gun = Tuesday, Ọjọ́rú = Wednesday, Ọjọ́bọ̀ = Thursday.

questions.stem: Àmàlà is made from
questions.explanation: Àmàlà is made from èlùbọ́.

questions.stem: Àkàrà is made from
questions.explanation: Àkàrà (bean cakes) are fried from ground beans.

questions.stem: Bojúbojú is a children's game of
questions.explanation: In Bojúbojú, one child covers his eyes while others hide.

questions.stem: "Ọmọ mẹ́ta" means
questions.explanation: mẹ́ta = three (when counting things).

questions.topic: Oja rira ati tita nile Yoruba (L2)
questions.stem: A trader calling out to customers to buy her goods is doing
questions.explanation: Ìpolówó ọjà is advertising/hawking goods.

questions.stem: In Yoruba marriage, the ceremony where the groom's family brings the bride price and gifts is called
questions.explanation: Ìdána is the bride price ceremony.

questions.stem: Ìkómọjáde refers to
options: bringing out a new baby (naming/outing ceremony)
questions.explanation: Ìkómọjáde is the ceremony of bringing the newborn out.

questions.stem: "Òjò ń rọ̀" means
questions.explanation: òjò = rain.

questions.stem: The masquerade festival among the Yoruba is
questions.explanation: Egúngún are ancestral masquerades.

questions.stem: The annual Ọ̀ṣun festival is celebrated in
questions.explanation: The Ọ̀ṣun-Òṣogbo festival takes place at the sacred grove in Òṣogbo.

questions.stem: Which of these is worn by Yoruba women on the head?
questions.explanation: Gèlè is the head-tie; fìlà is the man's cap.

questions.stem: Which of these shows personal hygiene?
options: Fífọ eyín ní àràárọ̀ (brushing teeth every morning)
questions.explanation: Brushing teeth daily keeps the body clean.

questions.stem: "Ọkọ̀ òfuurufú" is
questions.explanation: Ọkọ̀ òfuurufú = aeroplane; ọkọ̀ ojú-irin = train.

questions.stem: "Ìsìnkú" means
questions.explanation: Ìsìnkú is the burial of the dead.
